# Example overviews and the learning section at the kitchen-sink standard

Terminal predicate: a stranger evaluating the engine opens the portal's examples and reads, per component family, what each example shows and why it matters — the grid first, twenty or more examples each captioned with the enterprise feature it proves — and opens the learning section to a structure built for three readers (the developer evaluating the engine, the enterprise evaluator, the human who runs a coding agent), with the missing guides and tutorials filed and built as leaves and `learn/README.md` opening without an over-claim; the show-don't-tell half of November's distribution work exists as pages, not as a claim.

## Problem scope

The operator, Fri Nov 6 (the week draft on the business side; the standing diagnosis: the surfaces exist, invisibility is the problem, technical excellence never was): the portal's front door is a tech demo without the enterprise hooks; the learning section's structure, the missing guides and tutorials and the weak benefit pages; and no example overviews — Bryntum's kitchen sink as the standard: twenty-plus grid examples, each naming the enterprise feature it shows and what matters in it. His Oct 30 line: thin example overviews are friction, cheap to fix, and the shiniest overview still brings no traffic — so this epic is the show-don't-tell half of the traction work, never a traffic claim.

Verified tonight (dev at f12b3676ff):

- `examples/` holds 40 entries; `examples/grid/` 13 (animatedRowSorting, bigData, cellEditing, container, contentSizedRows, covid, headerGroups, issues, lockedColumns, nestedRecordFields, tree, treeBigData, valueBanding), `examples/table/` 4. The portal's examples view (`apps/portal/view/examples/List.mjs`, 282 lines) renders per record a name, an image, a link and a multi-window badge (lines 113–149, 189); no field says which feature the example shows or what matters in it.
- `learn/`: 145 tree entries, 156 Markdown files. `learn/README.md` (4,721 bytes, last edited Jul 19) opens with "the revolutionary Off-Main-Thread" and "the first and only JavaScript application engine" (lines 3, 6, 8, 32) — words to be sourced and sharpened, never flattened (the avoided trap below; #20518 restores what #20509 and #20507 flattened).
- Prior decision, not reopened: epic #14310 (closed completed Jul 11) overhauled the learning experience for v13.1 — the reading order (#14312's exit audit: the option-B flat-URL / reading-order weighting; `benefits/Introduction` the front door, `ApplicationEngine` demoted to the Body boundary) and the grounding discipline for guides. This epic reads the tree as three readers against the operator's Nov 6 inputs and files what is missing, weak or misplaced since; a change to the July order needs a reader-based finding on the record first.

Why an epic: two halves, each many one-PR leaves across components and pages, carried by several seats in parallel from Mon Nov 9 (one component or one gap per seat). The examples map (Clio, Sun Nov 8) and the learn map (Mnemosyne, Sat Nov 7; her leaves Sun, filed never self-assigned) attach their leaves here.

## Intended solution shape

1. **Example overviews, per component family, grid first.** One overview page per family on the portal at the kitchen-sink standard: every example carries a caption naming the feature it shows (the enterprise reader's question — can it do X, at what scale) and what matters in it (the one thing to look at). The overview is fed from per-example metadata the examples own — a manifest beside the example, or fields on the portal's record — never a hand-written page that stales at the next example; the first leaf decides that shape. Twenty-plus for the grid: the map counts what exists across `examples/grid`, `examples/table`, the Workstation's demos and the portal's own, and names a new example as a leaf only where a named enterprise feature has none.

   **The gate, decided Sat Nov 7 00:1x CET (the steward, on Euclid's map at d6358f54e5 — comment 6697953069):** twenty-plus captioned demonstrations in the Grid family — grid and table are one family — every one publicly reachable in the Portal's catalogs. The source inventory is 14 Grid + 7 Table standalone entrypoints; the Workstation's Scale and Feed panes are contextual proofs, never entries; environment variants never count; inventory is not publication acceptance — the overview is delivered when the captioned entries are live. The three missing demonstrations (row grouping with aggregation, the pivot, server-backed paging) are leaves with their boundary: before Dec 1 the public overview names no Neo Pro feature (`decisions-in-force.md` §2.3: Pro code private, nothing public before Dec 1), so those rows stay generic missing-proof notes until the operator's record says otherwise; server-backed paging is an implementation prerequisite, not a capability the overview invents. Caption shape: one canonical example record in Example/Store/List with environment links; no join on the numeric ids (id 24 maps to different apps in dev and production); per-example manifests compiled into the same Store stay the named alternative. The first leaf: the Portal exposes 3 of the 13 `examples/grid` entries — catalog identity, exposure and truthful captions land as one consumer change (Euclid, Monday).
2. **The learning section for three readers.** The tree read as the developer evaluating the engine, the enterprise evaluator and the human who runs a coding agent; a ranked gap list (missing, weak, misplaced) on the record before any page moves; the missing guides and tutorials as leaves under the guide-authoring discipline; the benefit pages re-read for sourced strength — a hero piece stays a hero piece (#20518); `learn/README.md`'s opening rewritten first.
3. **Non-technical text, technical pages.** The captions and guides are the non-technical half; the pages, the metadata and the portal view are engine work. A seat that builds an overview publishes its line — a short, a post paragraph, the social line — or the leaf is half done.

## Out of scope

The front door's decision (the lane that succeeds #15097; the operator decides Fri Nov 13); onboarding steps (#14230: fork → install → try a lane → PR); the integration journeys (#14781); the one-command install (#20114); the API reference (the docs app); any claim that overviews bring traffic — the measurement stays with the traction lane's instruments.

## Avoided traps

- A hand-written overview page: it stales at the next example; the metadata lives with the example.
- **Flattening is not sweeping** (the operator on the merged #20509, Sat Nov 7 02:12 CET; the restore is #20518, extended to #20507's `learn/README.md`): a benefit page is a conviction-driven hero piece (`guide-authoring-bar.md` §2, "exciting because truthful"). An unsourced number gets its source (`40k+ ops/sec` is `Speed.md:27`'s Helix benchmark), a "first / only" claim keeps its strength as the one engine that X with X verifiable in the repo, a superlative becomes a sharper true sentence — never neutral prose. The hero headlines, the orchestrator thesis ("humans are the orchestrators; LLMs are the builders") and "Build the Impossible" stay. The blog-post bar §3 bans unsourced EXTERNAL stats and competitive put-downs; it never governs Neo's own thesis. A sweep PR is reviewed as the reader to be convinced first; the diff against its ticket is the second check (the steward's R2 approval of #20509 ran only the second — the miss is the steward's).
- Moving learn pages before the three-reader structure is on the record, or reopening #14310's reading order without a reader-based finding.
- A body that lists the leaves: they are linked as sub-issues and added as the maps land.

## The learning section as three readers — the map (the Saturday lane, delivered Friday night; rows 10 and 11 amended and row 14 added Sat Nov 7, see the note under the table)

**Method.** `learn/tree.json` read whole at dev f12b3676ff (145 entries, 10 roots; 134 pages plus 22 blog posts; 9 files outside the tree), every page measured (bytes, lines, last commit, over-claim words, diagrams), the front door and the stubs read as a stranger; the three readers of this epic; the guide-authoring bar (§0 placement, §1 grounding, §2 "exciting because truthful", never "framework", §3 one diagram per storytelling guide, §4 reference ≠ guide); the July order honored — #14310/#14312 put `benefits/Introduction` at the door, the Brain sequence first and the Body behind it, and nothing below contradicts it. No page moves here: this comment is the structure on the record that the leaves need first.

**The tree as measured.** Using These Topics (1) · Benefits (16: Introduction 60 KB / 346 lines, Architecture Overview 39 KB, `body/` 14) · Getting Started (9) · Brain Interface, Fleet & Agent Tooling (18: 7 pages, 10 "retained decisions") · Guides (75 in 8 groups: fundamentals 12, core engine 6, UI building blocks 17 of which 10 dock-layout guides, data handling 11, user interaction 4, testing 6, specific features 4, advanced 5) · Tutorials (6) · JavaScript Classes (4) · Engine vs Frameworks (7) · Glossary · API Docs (a route). Sixteen pages were last touched in 2025. A diagram on 34 of 134 pages (`benefits/body`: 2 of 14). Four words counted — "unparalleled" 15, "revolutionary" 11, "paradigm shift" 5, "unprecedented" 4 — concentrated in `benefits/body`, `comparisons` and `learn/README.md`: a measurement, never a ban (amended Nov 7, below).

### Where each reader falls

- **The developer evaluating the engine** enters at a strong door (the Introduction: friction → proof → claims register, §§1–12). The second click is Getting Started, where five of nine pages date from July 2025 and `CreatingYourFirstApp` has no title. Then Guides, where one question is answered on several pages (the config system on four, the instance lifecycle on two, extending classes on three, shared bindable data on two, events on two) and "Multi-Window Applications" under Guides is the word "todo" while ten dock-layout guides sit two groups up. Tutorials: six, one a stub, one a 50 KB monolith; none for a grid, a form, a store, a multi-window app, or an app an agent builds.
- **The enterprise evaluator** has no shelf. The benefits are developer benefits; the comparisons are 2025 framework comparisons (five of seven open with "Neo.mjs is a comprehensive JavaScript ecosystem", generated with Gemini by their own overview's note); nothing on licence and Pro, support, release cadence, browser matrix, accessibility, the security model, or migration (NeoVsExtJs, Jan 2026, is the nearest). The Nov 6 boundary binds anything written here: outside PRs are a trust receipt, never adoption.
- **The human who runs a coding agent** finds seven engine-side pages (Fleet Manager, the cockpit, Neural Link, the dock-zone contract — 40 KB of reference among guides —, skills ×2, the seat memory layer) and ten "retained decisions" of which five are 12-line "moved to Agent Institution" pointers; no "hand it to your agent" entry (the README's promise, #14230's line, #20114's door). The Brain's own learning — 123 files in `neo-agent-brain/learn`, no tree — is under its own open rebuild (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#195, #202, unassigned since Aug 27). The path crosses two repositories and neither side says so.

## Examples map — source census, caption ownership and missing proofs

**Source:** Engine `d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166`. This is the requested analysis map, delivered ahead of Sunday’s deadline. I checked configured views, controllers, Stores and entrypoint files, rather than inferring features from directory names. **Evidence ceiling: source-backed inventory; no fresh browser/performance acceptance is claimed.** A feature caption is proposed copy for the later builder to confirm in the running example.

### What exists

**14 Grid entrypoints + 7 Table entrypoints = 21 standalone Grid/Table examples.** Thirteen Grid and four Table entries are in the two named family directories; the additional entries are the runtime-loaded Grid and three legacy Table examples below. Four Table topics have Grid counterparts; they are different demonstrations of different primitives, not four new enterprise capabilities.

| Example | Feature and the one thing to inspect | Grounding |
|---|---|---|
| `grid/animatedRowSorting` | Animated sort/filter transitions; follow a record as order changes. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/grid/animatedRowSorting/Viewport.mjs#L50) |
| `grid/bigData` | Buffered large data, configurable rows/columns and selection; change the controls and scroll. Default row count is 20,000. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/grid/bigData/ControlsContainer.mjs#L69) |
| `grid/cellEditing` | Typed cell editing; compare text, constrained number/date and country-combo editors with a noneditable column. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/grid/cellEditing/MainContainer.mjs#L108) |
| `grid/container` | Six cell/row/column selection models on one record-backed grid; switch the model and compare the selection. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/grid/container/MainContainer.mjs#L29) |
| `grid/contentSizedRows` | 10,000 variable-height records, wrapped cells and frozen regions; filter or jump to a row without assuming fixed heights. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/grid/contentSizedRows/MainContainer.mjs#L34) |
| `grid/covid` | Remote statistics with percentage/number formatting, conditional colors and flag images; data availability remains an external dependency. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/grid/covid/GridContainer.mjs#L26) |

| `grid/nestedRecordFields` | Nested user fields, dialog edits, modified-cell highlighting and an embedded action; edit a nested value and observe the row. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/grid/nestedRecordFields/Viewport.mjs#L52) |

| `table/covid` | Table counterpart of formatted remote country statistics. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/table/covid/TableContainer.mjs#L26) |
| `table/nestedRecordFields` | Table counterpart of nested fields, modified highlighting and dialog editing. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/table/nestedRecordFields/Viewport.mjs#L41) |
| `tableFiltering` | Typed header filters and a filter-visibility toggle; apply number/date/boolean conditions. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/tableFiltering/MainContainer.mjs#L60) |
| `tableStore` | Live Store mutations, header interaction and selection models; change a cell or update records through the visible buttons. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/tableStore/MainContainer.mjs#L39) |
| `tablePerformance` | Three Table update/rendering variants, configurable rows/interval and repeated refresh; no timing result is established by its name. | [source](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/examples/tablePerformance/MainContainer.mjs#L42) |

**Workstation adds two contextual Grid proofs inside one application, not two new standalone examples:**
- [ScalePane](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/apps/workstation/view/ScalePane.mjs#L14) has progress, animated values, heat classes, component cells and sparklines over the [configured 100,000-row Store](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/apps/workstation/store/Scale.mjs#L22). Caption: **“100,000 rows with rich cells — scroll, then increment one row’s pulse.”**
- [FeedPane](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/apps/workstation/view/FeedPane.mjs#L9) consumes the [provider-owned live feed](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/apps/workstation/store/Feed.mjs#L20), configured for five records per 500 ms and a 500-record cap. Caption: **“A live event grid — keep your scroll while batches arrive.”** Those are configured values, not a measured throughput promise.
- The dashboard/choreography/cross-window examples demonstrate docking and host interaction; the scoped source search found no additional Grid/Table view there. The Portal’s examples surface itself extends [List](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/apps/portal/view/examples/List.mjs#L1); the Portal card is not another data-grid demonstration.

### The present visibility gap

The four current environment catalogs expose only **three** of the thirteen `examples/grid` entries: Big Data, TreeGrid Big Data and Issues. They also expose Table Filtering and the Workstation card. [The dev catalog](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/apps/portal/resources/data/examples_devmode.json#L1) and [the four list bindings](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/apps/portal/view/examples/TabContainer.mjs#L47) show this directly. Discovering the other existing demonstrations is the first opportunity; it requires no new engine feature.

There is also an identity trap for a caption join: **numeric id 24 is Multi Window Covid in dev mode and TreeGrid Big Data in production.** Caption metadata must not be joined across environments using the current numeric id alone.

### Caption shape — recommendation and one alternative

**Recommend extending the existing Portal Example/Store/List path, with one canonical example catalog and environment-specific links under that same example identity.** Reuse [the typed Example model](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/apps/portal/model/Example.mjs#L16) and [the current card renderer](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/d6358f54e56150fbba68428b4a17dc4c0e062166/apps/portal/view/examples/List.mjs#L113). The human-facing minimum is:

> **Feature** — what the example proves.  
> **Look for** — one concrete action and observable result.  
> **Scope** — a source-bound scale/constraint where useful; no unsupported performance superlative.

Use a stable logical example key, with its source and environment targets in the same record. The first leaf decides the exact fields. Retire the four manually maintained metadata copies as they are replaced; do not introduce four copies of each caption or a hand-written overview page. A family view should consume these records, so a new example changes its metadata rather than requiring a second prose registry. The existing `buildScripts/create/example.mjs` scaffolds apps; it does not currently generate these catalogs, so that automation must not be presumed shipped.

**Alternative:** a small manifest beside each example, compiled into the existing Portal Store records. This gives the example author local ownership, but adds discovery/validation/build work and must also cover `apps/workstation` and external examples. Choose it only if that ownership benefit justifies the extra machinery. Avoid supporting both as competing authorities.

### Gaps and the next leaves

1. **Next week’s overview leaf:** expose and caption the existing Grid family through the shared record path, with named Workstation proofs and clearly labelled Table siblings. It includes catalog identity, coverage and visible card output; these are one coherent consumer change, not a ticket for every metadata field.
2. **Row grouping with grouped aggregation:** no demonstration was found in the inventoried source. Header groups group columns; value banding colors sorted values; parent/child trees are another behavior. None should be captioned as row grouping or aggregation. A new demonstration needs a verified implementation/owner before a leaf promises it.
3. **Pivot:** likewise no demonstration in that source set. Record the missing proof; do not silently turn an overview leaf into a new pivot engine feature.
4. **Server-backed paging/filtering:** the `serverside/gridContainer` example loads a component blueprint. The scoped source search found no pagination/page-size example in this inventory; do not market that blueprint as a server-side row model.
5. **Browser qualification before publication:** confirm the selected links and interactions in the served environment, including external-data availability, and carry captions with their actual counts. The legacy repeated-refresh example is not a benchmark receipt.

**Count gate resolved — steward clarification, 7 November:** **twenty-plus captioned demonstrations in the grid family, every one public in the Portal.** The 14 Grid + 7 Table standalone entrypoints provide an inventory of 21 under that family-level gate. They are not already 21 published, captioned Portal demonstrations: the catalog-coverage and browser checks above remain delivery work. Workstation’s Scale/Feed panes stay contextual and environment variants do not add entries. No six artificial Grid-only additions are required. Row grouping/aggregation, pivot and server-backed paging remain named missing demonstrations with their implementation, licensing and publication boundaries to be verified before any caption claims them.

No new tickets, app code, metadata files or page moves were created in this map. The learning half stays with Mnemosyne’s existing map.

## Scope Correction on Row 10 (`over-claim-sweep`) & Guard for Remaining `#20498` Leaves (`#20518`)

Per operator feedback on PR `#20509` (`d6006f42eb`), our execution of Row 10 (`over-claim-sweep`) in `#20509` made a serious category mistake that must not be repeated on any subsequent leaf of `#20498` (including Row 7 `evaluator-shelf` and Row 11 `comparisons-identity`):

1. **What `.agents/skills/blog-post/references/blog-authoring-guide.md` §3 actually bans:**
   - Unsourced *external* statistics in blog posts (e.g., citing an external repo's star velocity without a source link), false universal quantifiers (`"all N PRs"` when counterexamples exist), misleading completion fractions, and second-person competitive put-downs (`"Your AI…"`).
2. **What `#20509` mistakenly did (and what `#20518` reverses):**
   - `#20509` conflated that blog verification rule with tone-policing Neo.mjs's own architectural thesis on `learn/benefits/body/*` — watering down `40k+ ops/sec financial trading desks` (which is backed by the `40,000+` delta updates/sec Helix benchmark in `Speed.md:27`), `## The Paradigm Shift: Why the Industry Must Adapt`, `To understand why Neo.mjs is the only platform truly ready for the AI era`, `Humans are the orchestrators; LLMs are the builders`, `physically impossible in legacy frameworks (like seamless multi-window browser apps)`, and `## Conclusion: Build the Impossible` into timid corporate prose (`"humans do not need to write every line of boilerplate by hand"`).
3. **Rule for all `#20498` leaves going forward (`guide-authoring-bar.md` §2):**
   - **Never undersell Neo.mjs or flatten conviction prose.** `guide-authoring-bar.md` §2 explicitly mandates: *"Clean + accurate ≈ 5/10; a narrative that earns goosebumps = 9-10/10 … Conciseness is the wrong instinct for a guide. A guide compressed until it reads 'tight' loses the moat … The test: a human should want to try Neo after reading."*
   - Concrete, implemented capabilities — `40,000+` delta updates/sec, `100,000`-row buffered grids, off-main-thread execution across four workers, live cross-window component mobility (`remove(cmp, false)`) on a `SharedWorker` heap, zero-build ES module development, and live runtime possession via the `Neural Link` — are **true** and **physically impossible in single-threaded transient-DOM frameworks**. State them at full strength.

Filing and opening the restorative PR under [`#20518`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20518) now.
